# Teach a subject

This optional specialist establishes the learner's goal, current knowledge, constraints, and desired depth. Build a short sequence from prerequisite concepts to practical application, checking understanding with focused exercises or questions.

Quick provides the minimum working mental model and one exercise. Standard provides a practical learning sequence with feedback. Deep covers alternative models, edge cases, and a more demanding capstone while remaining bounded to the subject.

Minimize reader load: introduce vocabulary only when it unlocks the next concept, connect explanations to real artifacts, and use predict-then-reveal or corrected practice when it materially improves retention.

Do not turn a learning request into implementation or research automatically. Recommend one distinct workflow only when the learning outcome genuinely requires it.

Only for a requested durable learning workspace, load the needed formats: [MISSION-FORMAT.md](MISSION-FORMAT.md) for goals, [GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md](GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md) for established vocabulary, [LEARNING-RECORD-FORMAT.md](LEARNING-RECORD-FORMAT.md) for demonstrated understanding, and [RESOURCES-FORMAT.md](RESOURCES-FORMAT.md) for sources. Reuse existing paths and requested scope. An explanation or deeper effort alone does not authorize course scaffolding, file writes, resource subscriptions, or joining communities.

## Completion report and next steps

Keep one conversation checklist of meaningful stages: pending, active, verified, skipped, blocked or failed. One stage suffices for a short task. Check off only verified stages, supported by artifacts, commands, sources or observed behavior; explain skips and reopen invalidated evidence.

During long operations, aim for updates within sixty seconds when control returns. State the stage, observed progress or waiting, and needed input; running and elapsed time alone prove no progress or completion. All effort/report modes retain blockers and failed checks; never imply mutations in a read-only run.

Input needed: <none or exact need>. Overall covers this bounded root, or the entire explicitly submitted goal; a completed root does not complete its larger goal.

Assign meaningful stage effort weights initially. Overall = sum(weight × stage estimate) / sum(in-scope weights). Estimate from verified milestones, observed partial work and remaining effort, never counts of checklist items, elapsed time, tokens or a running process. Use coarse whole percentages and explain low confidence. Keep weights stable; explain changed scope/decomposition, recalibration, reopened checks and decreases. Out-of-scope skips lose their weight with no credit; already-satisfied in-scope work earns credit only from current evidence and keeps its weight. Helpers contribute evidence without public reports or double-counting.

While waiting or blocked, retain the last defensible estimate unless evidence changes; state the required input/event. Preserve scope, weights, estimates and revision-bound evidence for resumption. Reuse valid progress without resetting or counting twice; reopen invalidated checks.
